findings.title: Chunked-Encoding chunk footer is discarded without validating CRLF (request smuggling)
findings.evidence:
This tree is h11 0.14.0 (h11/_version.py:16), the version affected by CVE-2025-43859 / GHSA-vqfr-h8mv-ghfj. In ChunkedReader.__call__ the bytes that must terminate every chunk are represented only as an integer count, not as the required b"
": after the final byte of a chunk is consumed, line 197 sets `self._bytes_to_discard = 2`. On the next call, lines 163-170 execute `data = buf.maybe_extract_at_most(self._bytes_to_discard)` at line 164, then `self._bytes_to_discard -= len(data)` at line 167 and simply fall through once the counter reaches 0. There is no comparison of the extracted bytes against b"
", so any two attacker-supplied bytes (e.g. `XX`) are silently accepted in place of the mandatory chunk terminator. Reachability: any message framed with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` gets ChunkedReader via READERS[SEND_BODY]["chunked"] (h11/_readers.py:243), and the body bytes are fully attacker-controlled, so a peer sending `POST /one HTTP/1.1
Host: x
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

5
AAAAAXX45
0

GET /two ...` has h11 parse two requests where a strict/complementarily-lenient proxy parses one, the classic request-smuggling desync that lets an attacker bypass front-end authorization, poison caches, or capture another user's request/session. Upstream fixed this in 0.16.0 by storing the expected terminator (`self._bytes_to_discard = b"
"`) and raising LocalProtocolError when the received bytes differ (verified against the installed 0.16.0 h11/_readers.py lines 156-204). Note the advisory's precondition: h11 must sit behind a proxy whose own chunked parser has the complementary bug (it reads until EOL instead of requiring CRLF), so this is a malformed-framing acceptance root cause rather than a standalone unauthenticated RCE.
